title: Only the address field of the Executive Document may be modified after the Spell is deployed
content:
A.1.10.2.4.11.1.3 requires the Spell address to be added to the Executive Document by a new pull request, and states the constraint: "**Only the 'address' field in the Executive Document is permitted to be modified after the Spell has been deployed.**"

This is what makes the earlier hash meaningful. The document was hashed and merged in Step 8 (A.1.10.2.4.8.5.1) and used as the Reviewers' source of truth in Step 9. If arbitrary edits were possible afterwards, the reviewed reference and the published reference could differ, and nothing downstream would notice.

The single exception exists because the value is genuinely unknowable earlier — A.1.10.2.4.8.3.9 has all "$" placeholders replaced "except for the Spell address, which remains unknown at this stage," since the address only exists once the contract is deployed. The document is therefore complete-but-for-one-blank by construction, and the blank is filled by a mechanical fact rather than an editorial choice.

The verification is scoped to match: A.1.10.2.4.11.1.4 has any member of the Core Facilitator team "confirm that the 'address' field in the Executive Document has been updated with the correct Spell address" — one field, one question, no re-reading. A narrow permitted change makes a cheap and reliable check possible, which is the practical reason to prefer one mutable field over a general amendment power.

The residual risk is concentrated rather than eliminated: the address is the one thing an attacker would most want to change, since it redirects every voter to a different contract. That is why the field's review is mandatory even though the edit looks trivial.
description: A.1.10.2.4.11.1.3 freezes the reviewed document with exactly one exception — the one value that could not exist earlier — and a second Core Facilitator member verifies that field.
